added_lines: Gospel Reflection (Matthew 25:31-46) In the gospel today, Jesus gives us a powerful and moving of the final judgment. The Son of Man returns in glory and separates the sheep from the goats, not according to wealth, success, or even outward rel igious practices, but according to how they responded to those in need. Jesus ident ifies Himself with the hungry, thirsty, the stranger, the sick, and those impri soned, teaching us that whenever we show love and compassion to others, we are serving Him. This Gospel reminds us that faith is meant to be lived. It is easy to say that we love God, but Jesus invites us to make that love visible through acts of kindness, mercy, and generosity. The sheep are praised because their care for others flowed naturally from hearts shaped by God ʼs love. The challenge for us is not simply to avoid doing wrong, but to actively seek opportunities to do good. Every person in need is an opportun ity to encounter Christ and to share His love with the world. No act of kindness is ever too small in God ʼs eyes. A listening ear, an encouraging word, a helping hand, or a generous gi can become a sign of God ʼs presence in someone ʼs life. Let us ask the Lord to give us eyes that see the su �ering around us, hearts filled with compassion, and hands ready to serve. As we follow the ex ample of Jesus, who came not to be served but to serve, may we bring His love to t hose we meet Clonleigh (Strabane Pastoral Area)

each day. And when we stand before Him, may we hear those joyfu l words we all long to hear: “Well done, good and faithful servant” (Matthew 25:21). May the Lord ʼs grace guide us, His peace sustain us, and His blessing remain with us always. Amen. Remembering Our Deceased Loved Ones During November, we are especially encouraged to remember and pray for the faithful departed, t hose members of our families and dearly beloved who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith. As we pray for all our holy souls, we think also of all wh o grieve at this time. Prayer For All The Deceased God our Father, Your power brings us to birth, Your providence guides our lives, and by Your command we return to dust. Lord, those who die still live in Your presence, their lives change but do not end. I pray in hope for my family, relatives and friends, and for all the dead known to You alone. In company with Christ , who died and now lives, may they rejoice in Your kingdom, where all our tears are wiped away. Unite us together again in one family to sing Your praise fore ver and ever. May the Divine Assistance remain always with us, and may thes ouls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.
